# TD-470: `standards.md`'s "No AI signatures" is prose only — no config enforces it, and Igris never propagates the `attribution` setting to registered projects

## Metadata
- **Type:** Technical Debt · **Priority:** P2-Medium · **Effort:** S-Small
- **Status:** Ready · **Created:** 2026-09-24
- **Filed by:** the operator's ruling, 2026-09-24: "no ai signature on commits is a must."

## The finding

`core/os/standards.md:27` states the rule:

```
- **No AI signatures** — no "Generated with…", no Co-Authored-By tags.
```

That rule ships to every registered Igris project as prose the agent is expected to obey. Nothing enforces it:

1. **No gate checks it.** `core/git-hooks/commit-msg` gates acceptance criteria (TD-325) and agent-event coverage (FR-267); `pre-commit` gates the phase (PI-004). None of them looks at trailers. A `Co-Authored-By:` line commits clean.
2. **No config declared it.** Until today no `attribution` key existed in `~/.claude/settings.json` or in this repo's `.claude/settings.json`, so the harness had no machine-readable signal and fell back to its own default.
3. **Igris does not propagate it.** `cli/src/lib/json-merge.ts:19-20` documents the contract explicitly — the merge replaces `existing.hooks` and *"NO other top-level key is touched"*. `includeGitInstructions` is named there as a key Igris **preserves but never writes**. `attribution` would be treated the same: a project registered on a fresh machine gets Igris's hooks and none of its attribution posture.

Item 3 is the one that matters for the product, and it collides with the operator's founding principle (learning #1600): Igris is model-, harness- **and machine-**agnostic. A rule enforced only by a hand-edited `~/.claude/settings.json` on one laptop is precisely the kind of knowledge that does not travel.

## What was already done (2026-09-24, outside a hunt)

The immediate leak is closed on this machine and in this repo. `attribution` written to both scopes in the object form:

```json
"attribution": { "commit": "", "pr": "", "sessionUrl": false }
```

Schema confirmed against the installed binary (2.1.281), not from memory — its own description string reads: *"Each field defaults to the standard Claude Code attribution if not set. Set to false to hide all attribution, the same as `{ "commit": "", "pr": "", "sessionUrl": false }`. **Older Claude Code versions reject true or false here, so use the object form in settings files shared across versions.**"* The object form was chosen over the scalar `false` for exactly that reason — `.claude/settings.json` is tracked in git and travels to other machines and versions.

Note `includeCoAuthoredBy` is **deprecated**, superseded by `attribution` in Claude Code 2.0.62. Do not reach for it.

Also relevant: Claude Code **2.1.269** shipped *"Fixed the attribution reminder overriding a CLAUDE.md or memory rule against commit and pull request attribution."* This machine runs 2.1.281, so that fix is present — but the rule lives in `~/.igris/core/os/standards.md`, loaded through `/boot`, which is neither a CLAUDE.md nor a harness memory rule. The reminder this session received was the non-deferential variant (*"this replaces any earlier attribution guidance"*), consistent with the harness not recognising Igris's standard as a user instruction. **This is the general shape of the problem: Igris's OS text is invisible to the harness's own precedence rules.** Config is the only reliable channel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `attribution` (object form) is written into a registered project's `.claude/settings.json` by whatever Igris step owns that file, **without** breaching `json-merge.ts`'s "hooks only" contract — either by a deliberate, documented widening of that contract or by a separate writer. Whichever is chosen, `MAINTAINING.md`'s contract map records it.
- [ ] Re-running the write is idempotent, and a **user-set** `attribution` value is preserved, not clobbered — the same respect `json-merge.ts` gives user-owned hook entries. A project that deliberately wants a byline keeps it.
- [ ] A test proves the propagation with a **surviving control**: one fixture with no `attribution` gains it; one fixture with a user-chosen `attribution` keeps its own value unchanged. "All fixtures got the block" is not a measurement if nothing was designed to resist.
- [ ] A gate refuses a commit message carrying `Co-Authored-By:` or `Generated with` — so the standard is enforced where it is violated, not only where it is configured. Config covers the well-behaved harness; the gate covers every other path (a hand-typed commit, a different harness, a future model). **Both are needed:** config prevents, the gate catches.
- [ ] The gate's own test plants a real trailer in a real message file and asserts a non-zero exit, and plants a clean message and asserts silence.
- [ ] `core/os/standards.md:27` is updated to cite the enforcing mechanism, so the rule stops being unbacked prose.

## Out of scope

Retroactively rewriting history. 0 of the last 50 commits carry a trailer — the standard has held in practice — so there is nothing to clean up, and rewriting published history to enforce a style rule would cost far more than it returns.

## Risk

The gate is the risky half: it lands in `commit-msg`, which every registered project runs, and TD-469 is the fresh reminder that a mirror landing is a deploy. Build it behind the same discipline — repo first, runtime mirror as its own step, and an A/B on the live hook before and after (learning #1664), since a trailer gate's failure mode is refusing commits that should pass.

## Related

TD-469 / TD-468 (the mirror-is-a-deploy discipline, and the live-hook A/B) · learning #1600 (three-way agnosticism — the principle this violates) · `cli/src/lib/json-merge.ts` (the contract to widen or work around) · `core/os/standards.md:27` (the rule)
